content.text: You're trying to set up a digital store in Pakistan, but Stripe's restrictions are blocking your access. You're not alone. Many creators face the same problem in countries like Nigeria, Ghana, and Kenya. The solution lies in infrastructure sovereignty, where you own your store's backend and payment pipeline. In this guide, we'll show you how to set up a digital store that accepts crypto payments for free, using [[LINK:https://coremerch.[[LINK:https://coremerch.[[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/github-pages-free-digital-product-store-hosting-what-5|COREMERCH guide to github]].io/store/blog/github-pages-free-digital-product-store-hosting-what-6|GitHub Pages]].io/store/blog/how-supabase-order-database-digital-stores-complete-infrastructure-3|supabase]] as the order database and GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages for hosting.
Why This Infrastructure Works When Platforms Fail

When platforms fail or restrict access, your digital store's infrastructure must be able to adapt. By using GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages for hosting, Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script for backend logic, Supabase or Google Sheets for order storage, and NOWPayments for automatic on-chain crypto payment verification, you create a robust payment and delivery pipeline that's not dependent on any single platform. This infrastructure is designed to work even when platforms fail, ensuring your store remains live and operational.
What You Need Before You Deploy

Before deploying your digital store's infrastructure, you need to gather the necessary tools and resources. This includes a GitHub or Cloudflare account for hosting, a Supabase or Google Sheets account for order storage, and a NOWPayments account for automatic on-chain crypto payment verification. You'll also need to create a Sovereign Blueprint, which provides a complete set of documentation and source code for all 5 stacks, including NOWPayments integration and scaling playbooks.
Setting Up Your Payment and Delivery Pipeline

To set up your payment and delivery pipeline, you'll need to configure your NOWPayments account, create a Supabase table for orders, and connect your payment gateway to your Supabase instance. You'll also need to create a Cloudflare Pages or Google Apps Script function to handle payment verification and order storage. This pipeline will ensure that payments are processed automatically and orders are stored securely.
By using GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages for hosting, you can create a digital store that accepts crypto payments for free without relying on Stripe or any other payment platform.
Going Live and Processing Your First Transaction

Testing before promotion is not optional — it is the step that determines whether your store functions correctly under real conditions before real buyers encounter it. The test sequence has four steps. First: deploy the backend and confirm the webhook endpoint returns a valid response to a test HTTP POST. Second: configure the storefront and confirm the checkout displays correctly on desktop and mobile. Third: complete a real mainnet transaction with a small amount of actual crypto. Fourth: check your order database and confirm the order was logged correctly, the delivery email arrived, and the download link works.
Scaling Once the Infrastructure Is Running

The post-deployment ownership transfer is explicit in every COREMERCH deployment. When the build is complete and the end-to-end test passes, COREMERCH provides the credentials and configuration details for every component under the customer's accounts. The GitHub or Cloudflare repository is under the customer's account from the start. The Supabase or Google Sheets database is under the customer's account. The NOWPayments account is under the customer's email. COREMERCH removes collaborator access upon delivery. From that point, the store runs entirely under the customer's own accounts.
